newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba-Flexibility the answer to German unemployment.
newsitem.headline: Buba-Flexibility the answer to German unemployment.

text.p: A continuation of moderate wage increases and the dismantling of structural restrictions are just as important as an economic recovery for improvement in the German job market, the Bundesbank said on Tuesday.
The central bank noted that steps taken in the chemicals sector to promote job-creation measures for the long-term unemployed along with trainee programmes had not been taken up elsewhere.

The Bundesbank said there was an insufficient flexibility of working time and a lack of wage differentiation, suggesting that wages should be freed up to allow salaries to be paid below the pay scale rate, a practice which it noted was already being adopted in the former East German states.
By the end of November the number of seasonally adjusted registered unemployed in Germany was at 4.1 million, up 365,000 on the year before.
